headline: 7 top Awami League leaders sentenced to death for crimes against humanity
summary: The International Crimes Tribunal has issued the death penalty for seven leaders of the banned Awami League and its associate organizations over atrocities during the July uprising.
details: The International Crimes Tribunal has sentenced seven leaders of the banned Awami League and its affiliate organizations to death for crimes against humanity committed during the July mass uprising.
The convicted leaders include high-profile figures such as Obaidul Quader, Syed Nayem Ahmed, and others associated with the youth and student wings of the party.

In addition to the death penalty, the tribunal has ordered that half of the assets of five specific leaders—including Quader and others—be sold to provide compensation to the victims of the July atrocities.
The Chief Prosecutor stated that the trial proceeded according to legal provisions, even for those defendants who were intentionally absconding from the court.
Defense lawyers for the convicted leaders have expressed dissatisfaction with the verdict, claiming the judgment is not based on sufficient evidence.
The Home Minister commented that a single cocktail explosion during the announcement of the verdict did not diminish the significance of the latest ruling.
caption:
7 top Awami League leaders sentenced to death for crimes against humanity. Half of their assets are to be sold for victim compensation.

The International Crimes Tribunal has sentenced seven leaders of the banned Awami League and its affiliate organizations to death for crimes against humanity committed during the July mass uprising.

The convicted leaders include high-profile figures such as Obaidul Quader, Syed Nayem Ahmed, and others associated with the youth and student wings of the party.

In addition to the death penalty, the tribunal has ordered that half of the assets of five specific leaders—including Quader and others—be sold to provide compensation to the victims of the July atrocities.

The Chief Prosecutor stated that the trial proceeded according to legal provisions, even for those defendants who were intentionally absconding from the court.

Defense lawyers for the convicted leaders have expressed dissatisfaction with the verdict, claiming the judgment is not based on sufficient evidence.

The Home Minister commented that a single cocktail explosion during the announcement of the verdict did not diminish the significance of the latest ruling.

Source: Dhaka Tribune, Prothom Alo, Jamuna TV

headline: DU students trample photos of Jinnah and Ghulam Azam at DUCSU
summary: Students pasted images of the two figures on the floor of the DUCSU building and museum to express their protest.
details: Students of Dhaka University trample photos of Muhammad Ali Jinnah and Ghulam Azam on September 15.
The incident took place in front of the Dhaka University Central Students' Union (DUCSU) building and inside the DUCSU museum.
The students pasted the images of the two figures on the floor to deliberately walk over them as a form of protest.
This action was carried out during the afternoon of September 15.
